title: Augmented simplicial object of a counital coassociative endofunctor
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be an ordinary category, $T:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ an endofunctor, and $e:T\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}$ and $c:T\to T^2$ natural transformations satisfying $(eT)\circ c=1_T=(Te)\circ c$ and $(cT)\circ c=(Tc)\circ c$. For $n\geq0$ set $B_n=T^{n+1}$, with $T^0=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}$. The natural transformations $d_i=T^i e T^{n-i}:B_n\to B_{n-1}$ for $n\geq1$, $0\leq i\leq n$, and $s_i=T^i c T^{n-i}:B_n\to B_{n+1}$ for $0\leq i\leq n$, make $B_\bullet$ a simplicial object [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object] in the category of endofunctors of $\mathcal C$. The map $e:B_0\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}$ extends to an augmentation $B_\bullet\to\operatorname{const}(\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C})$. In particular evaluation at $x\in\mathcal C$ gives an augmented simplicial object, naturally in $x$.

source.place: Tag 0G5N, lemma-godement, with the construction in Example 0G5M (example-godement).

proof.text: Write $1_a$ for the identity transformation on $T^a$, including $1_0$ on the identity functor, and write $\star$ for horizontal composition. Thus $d_i^n=1_i\star e\star1_{n-i}$ and $s_i^n=1_i\star c\star1_{n-i}$. These are natural transformations because whiskering a naturality square by a functor again gives a naturality square. We use the interchange identity $(\alpha'\circ\alpha)\star(\beta'\circ\beta)=(\alpha'\star\beta')\circ(\alpha\star\beta)$. To verify it directly, define $(\alpha\star\beta)_x=\alpha_{G'x}\circ F(\beta_x)$ for $\alpha:F\to F'$ and $\beta:G\to G'$. Expand the right side at $x$, move $F'(\beta'_x)$ past $\alpha_{G'x}$ using naturality of $\alpha$ at $\beta'_x$, and use functoriality of $F$. The result is $(\alpha'\circ\alpha)_{G''x}\circ F((\beta'\circ\beta)_x)$, the left side. Horizontal composition is associative with these component formulas, and identities compose to identities; hence parentheses can be suppressed.

source.place: Tag 0G5N opening calculation; interchange of Tag 003F (categories-lemma-properties-2-cat-cats), here verified directly from naturality.

proof.text: Face--face relations: for $n\geq1$ and $0\leq i<j\leq n+1$, expand both $d_i^n\circ d_j^{n+1}$ and $d_{j-1}^n\circ d_i^{n+1}$ and apply interchange from step 1. Each becomes $1_i\star e\star1_{j-i-1}\star e\star1_{n+1-j}$. Thus $d_i d_j=d_{j-1}d_i$. In the boundary case $j=i+1$ the middle identity is $1_0$, so the calculation still applies.

source.place: Tag 0G5N, lemma-godement, proof; notation from Example 0G5M.

proof.text: Mixed relations away from the duplicated factor: for $n\geq2$ and $0\leq i<j\leq n-1$, both $d_i^n\circ s_j^{n-1}$ and $s_{j-1}^{n-2}\circ d_i^{n-1}$ reduce by interchange to $1_i\star e\star1_{j-i-1}\star c\star1_{n-j-1}$. For $0\leq j$ and $j+1<i\leq n$, both $d_i^n\circ s_j^{n-1}$ and $s_j^{n-2}\circ d_{i-1}^{n-1}$ reduce to $1_j\star c\star1_{i-j-2}\star e\star1_{n-i}$. Every displayed exponent is nonnegative in its stated range.

source.place: Tag 0G5N, lemma-godement, proof; notation from Example 0G5M.

proof.text: Mixed relations at the duplicated factor: for $n\geq1$ and $0\leq j\leq n-1$, interchange rewrites $d_j^n\circ s_j^{n-1}$ as $1_j\star((e\star1_1)\circ c)\star1_{n-j-1}$ and $d_{j+1}^n\circ s_j^{n-1}$ as $1_j\star((1_1\star e)\circ c)\star1_{n-j-1}$. The two counit hypotheses identify both with the identity on $T^n=B_{n-1}$. This includes $n=1$, so the two faces after the degree-zero degeneracy both give $1_{B_0}$.

source.place: Tag 0G5N, lemma-godement, proof; notation from Example 0G5M.

proof.text: Degeneracy--degeneracy relations: fix $n\geq1$, $0\leq i\leq j\leq n-1$. If $i<j$, interchange makes both $s_i^n\circ s_j^{n-1}$ and $s_{j+1}^n\circ s_i^{n-1}$ equal to $1_i\star c\star1_{j-i-1}\star c\star1_{n-j-1}$. If $i=j$, these composites are respectively $1_i\star((c\star1_1)\circ c)\star1_{n-i-1}$ and $1_i\star((1_1\star c)\circ c)\star1_{n-i-1}$. Coassociativity identifies them. This proves the fifth simplicial relation, including the adjacent duplication in degree zero.

source.place: Tag 0G5N, lemma-godement, proof; notation from Example 0G5M.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-simplicial-operators-reconstruction] to $\mathcal D=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C,\mathcal C)$, $U_n=B_n$ and the specified natural transformations. Steps 2--5 establish each of its five relations in every defined degree. Its reconstruction clause gives a simplicial object with precisely these degree objects and operators. No limits, colimits, or smallness of $\mathcal C$ are needed: functors and transformations are taken in a containing universe.

source.place: Tags 0G5N opening proof sentence and 016B(2), lemma-characterize-simplicial-object.

proof.text: Define $A_n:B_n\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}$ as the horizontal composite of $n+1$ copies of $e$, so $A_0=e$. For $n\geq1$, interchange yields $A_{n-1}\circ d_i^n=A_n$: the deleted factor contributes $e$ and every other factor contributes its existing copy of $e$. Moreover $A_{n+1}\circ s_i^n$ is the horizontal composite of copies of $e$ with $(e\star e)\circ c$ in position $i$. Since $e\star e=e\circ(e\star1_1)$ by interchange, the counit equation gives $(e\star e)\circ c=e$. Hence $A_{n+1}\circ s_i^n=A_n$ for all $n\geq0$.

source.place: Tag 0G5N, lemma-godement, proof; notation from Example 0G5M.

proof.text: The constant simplicial object with value $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}$ sends every operator to its identity. The face and degeneracy equations of step 7 therefore say exactly that the family $A_n$ commutes with its faces and degeneracies. The morphism clause of [lem-trf-simplicial-operators-reconstruction] gives an augmentation $B_\bullet\to\operatorname{const}(\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C})$, whose degree-zero component is $e$.

source.place: Tag 0G5N last paragraph and Tag 016B(3), lemma-characterize-simplicial-object.

proof.text: Evaluate the constructed functor and augmentation at $x\in\mathcal C$. Evaluation preserves identities and composition componentwise, so the simplicial functor laws and augmentation squares remain valid. For a morphism $f:x\to y$, the degree maps $T^{n+1}(f)$ commute with every simplicial operator and with $A_n$ by naturality of those transformations; identities and composites of $f$ are preserved by each $T^{n+1}$. Thus the evaluated augmented simplicial object is natural in $x$.

source.place: Tag 0G5N, lemma-godement, proof; notation from Example 0G5M.

lean.statement: theorem comonad_simplicial_object {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (T : C ⥤ C) (e : T ⟶ 𝟭 C) (c : T ⟶ T ⋙ T) (h₁ : c ≫ Functor.whiskerRight e T ≫ (Functor.leftUnitor T).hom = 𝟙 T) (h₂ : c ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft T e ≫ (Functor.rightUnitor T).hom = 𝟙 T) (h₃ : c ≫ Functor.whiskerRight c T ≫ (Functor.associator T T T).hom = c ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft T c) : ∃ (B : SimplicialObject (C ⥤ C)) (α : B ⟶ (SimplicialObject.const (C ⥤ C)).obj (𝟭 C)), (∀ n : ℕ, B.obj (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk n)) = NaturalTransport.power T (n + 1)) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 2)), HEq (B.δ i) (Functor.whiskerLeft (NaturalTransport.power T (n + 1 - i.val)) (Functor.whiskerRight e (NaturalTransport.power T i.val)))) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1)), HEq (B.σ i) (Functor.whiskerLeft (NaturalTransport.power T (n - i.val)) (Functor.whiskerRight c (NaturalTransport.power T i.val)))) ∧ HEq (α.app (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk 0))) e ∧ ∃ E : C ⥤ SimplicialObject.Augmented C, E ⋙ SimplicialObject.Augmented.drop = B.flip ∧ E ⋙ SimplicialObject.Augmented.point = 𝟭 C ∧ ∀ (x : C) (n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ), HEq ((E.obj x).hom.app n) ((α.app n).app x)
lean.note: Reuses CategoryTheory.NaturalTransport.power through definition node def-trf-endofunctor-powers. HEq specifies the literal whiskered operators across equal parenthesized power functors; it is equality, not an arbitrary comparison isomorphism. Evaluation is a functor to Mathlib augmented simplicial objects.
